clue.text: Numbers say — and say rudely — "There aren't many flowers here"

parts.note: say, as in 'for example', gives EG

indicators.note: done rudely, roughly, the letters of the second say are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone with a mouth on them complains loudly that there is hardly a bloom in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rudely' scrambles SAY into AYS. The definition is cryptic in a quiet way: a small posy is a place where there are only a few flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A posy is a small bunch of blooms, so it is a spot holding only a few of them.

clue.text: Stupid fellow is blocking most of Hawaiian island

indicators.note: the short pieces block the island's name by sitting inside it
most of a word means it loses its final letter here

parts.note: Oahu is the Hawaiian island holding Honolulu

explanation.surface: A dim man is standing in the way on a Hawaiian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupid fellow' looks like a single unit giving OAF, but 'Stupid' is the definition and the fellow is only F; 'most of' drops the island's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oafish describes a clumsy lout, someone slow-witted and dull.

clue.text: Temperature from historic times had an effect

parts.note: the old days are historic times, giving OLD

explanation.surface: The weather in bygone days made its mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that told on a person showed its effect on them, as strain tells.

clue.text: Work done at home source of concern for the USA, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way
the source of a word is where it starts, so its first letter is taken

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Domestic chores are worrying for Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles the first letter of 'concern' with FOR and THEUSA into the ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Housecraft is skill in running a household: cooking, cleaning and the like.

clue.text: Speech cut? This looks bad, stupid

indicators.note: cut here means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an idiom is a manner of speech

indicators.note: something that looks bad is out of shape, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone frets that a cut in a speech will make it look poor and foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims IDIOM to IDIO; 'looks bad' turns THIS into TISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotish is an informal adjective for foolish, behaving like an idiot.

clue.text: Country making no progress has to ditch male in leading position

indicators.note: ditch means drop, so the named part is removed

parts.note: stagnation is a state of no progress
a stag is a male deer, and here it sits at the start of the word

explanation.surface: A stuck country must remove the man at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: STAGNATION loses STAG from its front. 'making' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation is a state or people, which is what country means here.

clue.text: Icy expanse escaping first shot

parts.note: polar regions are icy, so icy suggests POLAR

indicators.note: the opening letter escapes, so it is dropped

parts.note: a void is an empty expanse

explanation.surface: A photograph is taken as someone gets away from a sheet of ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaping first' trims VOID to OID.
explanation.definitionFit: A Polaroid is an instant photograph, so a single shot from that camera.

clue.text: Party debut for miss in old cloak

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the debut, or first appearance, of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A young woman makes her first appearance at a party in a vintage cape.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a loose hooded cloak worn with a mask at masquerades.

clue.text: Tricorne that's corny?

parts.note: a tricorne is literally a hat from long ago, and the phrase also means stale or clichéd

explanation.surface: Asking whether a three-cornered hat is a tired joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The literal reading, an antique hat, and the idiom, out of date, meet in one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for tired or unoriginal, and a tricorne is quite literally headwear of a bygone age.

clue.text: Stop a satellite beginning to decay

parts.note: a, as in 'per' (ten pounds a head), gives PER
Io is a moon of Jupiter

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Halt a moon before it starts to rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' meaning each is PER, as in 'twice a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Period is the American term for a full stop, the dot ending a sentence.

clue.text: Fail to apprehend drunk accompanying one regretful lady

indicators.note: apprehend means seize, so the word holds the others inside

parts.note: to fail to hit is to miss

indicators.note: accompanying puts the numeral beside the drinker

parts.note: a sot is a drunk
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Police fail to arrest a drunk who has company, leaving one woman sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: SOTI sits inside MISS. 'Miss Otis Regrets' is a Cole Porter song in which the lady sends apologies that she cannot come to lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter's song title is 'Miss Otis Regrets', so its heroine is a woman expressing sorrow.

clue.text: Coping badly with heat, leading to disease

indicators.note: done badly, the letters are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: Struggling with high temperatures makes people ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles COPING and HEAT together; 'with' only links them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathogenic means capable of causing illness, as germs are.

clue.text: Refuse to remain with enterprise

explanation.surface: Declining to stay put shows initiative.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a verb phrase it means quit the place; as a noun it is drive and gumption.

clue.text: Some raucous noise reflected current elements

indicators.note: reflected, as in a mirror, means read backwards
some of the words means only a run of letters inside them is taken

explanation.surface: A harsh racket bounced back by the latest components.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes SNOI from 'raucous noise' and 'reflected' turns it round. 'current' is electric current, not the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: Ions are charged particles that carry an electric current through a solution.

clue.text: Religion accordingly includes suggestion

indicators.note: includes means the word holds the other inside

parts.note: so, as in 'and so', means accordingly
a hint is a suggestion

explanation.surface: A faith is said to carry an implied message.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the indigenous faith of Japan, honouring spirits called kami.

clue.text: Old warship, smooth around shore, avoiding North

parts.note: to iron something is to smooth it
C, short for circa, means around

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving out, and North is N

parts.note: land is the shore as seen from the sea

explanation.surface: An old warship steers a smooth course round the coast, keeping out of northern waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding North' takes N out of LAND, leaving LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironclads were nineteenth-century warships armoured with iron plates.

clue.text: Certainly poor performer is touring a county town

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word encircles the a

parts.note: OK is an informal yes, certainly
a ham is an overacting, poor performer

explanation.surface: A bad actor is definitely on tour round a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: OAKHAM is the county town of Rutland, England's smallest county.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakham is the administrative seat of Rutland, so it is that county's main town.

clue.text: Individual, by turning up, interrupting magazine? Its content is ready

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so these letters go inside

parts.note: one is a single individual

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

explanation.surface: Someone appears and breaks into a magazine, wondering if its contents are finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is old slang for cash, as in 'the ready', so the definition describes what the bag holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A money bag holds cash, and 'the ready' is old slang for ready money.

clue.text: Reduced European capital to support work, heading off drilling site

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other
with its heading off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: toil is hard work

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: A shrunken European capital is propping up an enterprise that has lost its leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' trims RIGA to RIG and 'heading off' cuts TOIL to OIL; 'to support' puts RIG under OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil rig is the platform from which wells are bored into the seabed.

clue.text: Old players returning for City

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the LSO, the London Symphony Orchestra, is a band of players

explanation.surface: Veteran musicians come back to town.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway, a major urban centre.

clue.text: Sailor heads off upwards, securing a lanyard's end

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so these letters go inside
in a down clue, upwards means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: to head off is to go, so heads off gives GOES

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A sailor climbs aloft, tying off the tip of a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upwards' turns GOES into SEOG, which holds A and D.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea dog is an old, experienced sailor.

clue.text: Nonplussed after conclusion of argument, having no leeway

indicators.note: after puts the first piece behind the second

parts.note: the point is what an argument arrives at
someone nonplussed looks blank

explanation.surface: Someone baffled once a debate ends, with no room to manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Point-blank range is so close there is no margin for error, and a point-blank refusal allows no wiggle room.

clue.text: Just the one academic doing for English or American writer

indicators.note: doing for means replacing, so one piece takes the other's place

parts.note: lone means single, just the one
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A single scholar is killing off a writer from one of two countries.
explanation.walkthrough: In LONE, DON replaces E. 'English or' makes you hunt for a British writer, but 'English' only gives the letter. Jack London wrote 'The Call of the Wild'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack London was a US novelist, author of 'White Fang' and 'The Call of the Wild'.

clue.text: Flying of crane interrupted by large bird handler

indicators.note: interrupted by means the other letter breaks in
flying, here sent scattering, means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crane's flight is cut short by a bigger bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' scrambles OF CRANE, and L goes inside to give the full word.
explanation.definitionFit: A falconer trains and flies hawks and falcons for hunting.

clue.text: Loves calls for attention, keeping working

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the word contains the other

parts.note: hey is a cry to get attention, so the plural gives HEYS
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Sweethearts shout to be noticed while still busy at their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey is an endearment, so honeys are darlings or sweethearts.

clue.text: Hot boiling oil in Indian festival

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: boiling means seething and churned up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Sizzling hot oil being used at a Hindu celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boiling' turns OIL into OLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colours, when people throw coloured powder.

clue.text: With higher award initially received, medal is to be neglected

definitions.note: the definition is a base-form verb phrase, matching the idiom 'go hang'

indicators.note: received means taken inside, so the letters go into the word

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A medal given with a senior honour attached is to be cast aside.
explanation.walkthrough: HA, the first letters of 'higher award', goes into GONG. 'is to' only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Let something go hang means not caring what becomes of it, so leaving it uncared for.

clue.text: Part of Scotland cheerful, having received grant

indicators.note: having received means holding the other inside

parts.note: gay in its older sense means cheerful
to allow something is to grant it

explanation.surface: A region of Scotland is in good spirits after getting funding.
explanation.definitionFit: Galloway is a region in the south-west of Scotland, a historic area there.
